hook_text: A factory sells bricks. A village pays in lungs. The invoice? It was never printed.
clip_script: Picture a small factory beside a river, upstream from a village. Brick buyers pay for bricks; the owner pays for clay and wages. Everyone in the deal is happy. But the kiln smoke drifts over the village, and the wash-water runs into the river where children swim. The village coughs — and the village was never part of the deal. They pay a cost that appears on nobody's invoice. And here is the trap: because the brickmaker never pays that bill, bricks are priced too cheap, so the market cheerfully orders more bricks — and more smoke — than it would if the full cost showed on the tag. The pollution is not the market malfunctioning; it is the market working perfectly on prices that lie.
visual_style: A split screen: a till printing receipts for bricks on one side; on the other, an invisible receipt materialising over the village, itemising cough, garden, river — then stamped UNPAID.
mood: Quiet outrage building to the twist line.
pacing: Gentle storybook opening, a beat of silence at 'never part of the deal', then the twist delivered slowly.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson: how taxes, owners and treaties make the polluter finally pay.
